cards.title: Moss Message Observatory Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led writing table for decoding secret nature notes in fiction: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Set out green crayons and one paper porch-light card per writer; the signal exists only on the page: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Invent a moss code, then use it to start a short observatory scene: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: On the paper porch-light front, draw three moss symbols that mean: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: On the back, explain the secret moss message in one sentence: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: The observatory helper spots a moss message glowing on the signal card: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The moss letters changed when ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Add one clue that makes the message easier to understand: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle one moss mark and write what it whispers: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Ask an adult to trade one pretend signal word with you: ____________________.

cards.title: Tidepool Timekeepers Lab Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led practice for beginning, middle, and ending order with lab helpers and tiny tidepool clocks: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Place three blank slips labeled first, next, and last beside each paper card: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Make a tidepool clock signal, then write what changes at each step: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: On the paper porch-light front, sketch a tidepool clock showing first, next, last: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: On the back, write what each clock mark means: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: A lab timekeeper taps the signal card when the tidepool clock says: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The tiniest clock in the lab clicked because ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Add a middle step so the change makes sense: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write one soft lab sound the clock makes: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Tell an adult the three-step signal in order: ____________________.

cards.title: Revision River Ferry Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led draft practice for swapping weak words for sharper story details: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Give each writer a draft sentence and a paper porch-light ferry card with three clearer-detail spaces: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Pretend the ferry carries one sentence across Revision River, improving it at each dock: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: On the paper porch-light front, write the sentence before the ferry fixes it: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: On the back, write the stronger ferry version: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: The ferry captain raises the signal card when one sentence needs: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The ferry would not leave until ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Replace one plain word with a word that gives a clearer picture: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Underline the word you changed and write the new word: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Show an adult one sentence before and after: ____________________.

cards.title: Clue Label Tower Museum Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led writing for museum mystery labels that make readers ask useful questions: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Set out small paper label strips and one porch-light card, then invent a pretend museum object: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Name one object, hide one clue in its label, then write the scene: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: On the paper porch-light front, draw a museum label with one missing fact: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: On the back, write the question a visitor should ask: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: At the tower museum, the signal card points to a label that asks: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The label on the tallest shelf asked ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Add one clue that points to the answer without saying it: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the mystery question for now: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Ask an adult to answer your label question with a silly guess: ____________________.

cards.title: Compass Craft Academy Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led setting practice before a character acts: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Give each writer a paper compass rose and a porch-light card, then pick one academy zone from the page list: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Spin your pencil over the compass rose, choose one direction word, and build a craft-academy scene from it: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: On the paper porch-light front, mark the compass word that opens the scene: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: On the back, list two setting details for that academy zone: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: The craft academy signal points the character toward a place called: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The compass needle pointed to the craft table where ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Add one sound, smell, or texture to make the setting clearer: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write the compass word and one object beside it: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Tell an adult which setting detail changed the scene: ____________________.

cards.title: Binding Day Boardwalk Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led ending practice for a handmade mini story: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Fold two sheets into a booklet and add one paper porch-light ending card for a fiction-only table scene: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Choose how the final signal glows, then write the ending and a title: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: On the paper porch-light front, draw the final signal shape for Binding Day: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: On the back, write what changed by the last page: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: At the boardwalk binder booth, the last signal means: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: On Binding Day, the booklet would be finished after ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Add one ending detail that shows how the character feels now: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write the final sentence first: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Read an adult your ending and ask for one kind word to add: ____________________.
